rack_air_gpu.name: Air GPU Rack
rack_air_gpu.description: Four 8-GPU servers breathing cold-aisle air through hot-aisle fans. About 40 kW is where air cooling runs out of breath, so keep a CRAH within reach.

rack_dlc_gpu.name: Liquid-Cooled GPU Rack
rack_dlc_gpu.description: A 72-GPU NVLink rack with cold plates on every die, drawing around 120 kW. Roughly 80% of its heat leaves through the coolant loop; the rest still needs air.

rack_storage.name: Storage Rack
rack_storage.description: Dense NVMe and disk shelves holding the datasets and checkpoints that training jobs stream from. No FLOPS, but without enough terabytes, big jobs stall.

crah_unit.name: CRAH Unit
crah_unit.description: A computer-room air handler with its own compressor: it pulls hot air from nearby aisles and returns it at about 20°C. Simple and reliable, but its fans and compressor run whether the racks are busy or not.

chiller.name: Chiller
chiller.description: Rejects coolant-loop heat outdoors, spending about 1 kW of electricity for every 5.5 kW it moves. Its efficiency drops on hot afternoons, so basements and roofs suit it best.

cdu.name: Coolant Distribution Unit
cdu.description: A heat exchanger and pump skid that feeds warm-water cold plates from the facility loop with a ~4°C approach. A coolant loop carries no more rack heat than its CDUs can pass.

grid_tie.name: Grid Tie
grid_tie.description: Utility substation and step-down transformer. It imports up to 1.5 MW at the going rate, which is cheap at night and painful during the evening peak.

genset.name: Diesel Genset
genset.description: An 800 kW backup generator that cranks automatically when the net runs short and takes about ten minutes to reach load. Every kWh it makes is expensive.

ups_battery.name: UPS Battery Bank
ups_battery.description: Lithium-ion strings behind a double-conversion UPS: 250 kWh that bridges the gap until the genset is up. About 5% is lost in conversion.

parts_depot.name: Parts Depot
parts_depot.description: Shelving for spare GPU trays, PSUs and pumps. Failures are routine at scale, so a well-stocked depot close to the racks keeps repair times short.

bot_charger.name: Bot Charging Dock
bot_charger.description: Home base for maintenance rovers. Two bays, each charging at 5 kW, and new bots are delivered here.
